author: trellixvulnteam
body:
# Patching CVE-2007-4559

Hi, we are security researchers from the Advanced Research Center at [Trellix](https://www.trellix.com). We have began a campaign to patch a widespread bug named CVE-2007-4559. CVE-2007-4559 is a 15 year old bug in the Python tarfile package. By using extract() or extractall() on a tarfile object without sanitizing input, a maliciously crafted .tar file could perform a directory path traversal attack. We found at least one unsantized extractall() in your codebase and are providing a patch for you via pull request. The patch essentially checks to see if all tarfile members will be extracted safely and throws an exception otherwise. We encourage you to use this patch or your own solution to secure against CVE-2007-4559. Further technical information about the vulnerability can be found in this [blog](https://www.trellix.com/en-us/about/newsroom/stories/research/tarfile-exploiting-the-world.html).

If you have further questions you may contact us through this projects lead researcher [Kasimir Schulz](mailto:kasimir.schulz@trellix.com).

author: ncooke3
body:
Add support for targets with mixed language sources.

### Motivation:

At the time of this PR, the package manager [does not support targets with mixed language sources](https://github.com/apple/swift-package-manager/blob/ce099264a187759c2f587393bd209d317a0352b4/Sources/PackageLoading/TargetSourcesBuilder.swift#L183-L189). This feature was motivated by the need for packages to contain mixed language sources for legacy and technical reasons.

### Modifications:

Detailed design is explained in https://github.com/apple/swift-evolution/pull/1895

The diff is large but most of it comes from the suite of integration tests. I added many fixture tests to test many cases that arise when making a mixed target.

#### High Level Overview
1. Added a `MixedTarget` type to model targets with mixed language sources 
    - The current approach is to effectively wrap a `SwiftTarget` and `ClangTarget`.
1. Added a `MixedTargetBuildDescription` type to model how `MixedTarget`'s should build.
    - The current approach is to effectively wrap a `SwiftTargetBuildDescription` and `ClangTargetBuildDescription`.
1. Expanded upon the existing `VFSOverlay` type to support VFS overlay directories.
    - Used by `MixedTargetBuildDescription` when creating the VFS overlays needed to compile a mixed language target.
1. Expanded upon the existing `ModuleMapGenerator` implementation to generate module maps for mixed language targets. This involves adding a submodule to the module map to expose the generated Swift interop header.
1. Modify the `PackageBuilder` to created a mixed language target instead of throwing an error when mixed language sources are detected (when sufficient Swift tools version is detected).
1. Add unit tests to test planning a mixed target, mixed target module map generation, and building a mixed target.
1. Add extensive suite of integration (in `FunctionalTests` target) tests to test mixed target use cases.

### Result:

Targets with mixed language sources can be built, tested, and depended on by other packages.

---

### Development Workflow

I have added info to [this](https://docs.google.com/document/d/1LkZiRCqGD4j9NYJ0fLHP_NGhUQumzYbtQLYlq_cYGss/edit?usp=sharing&resourcekey=0-DB_FlMh9Z7inEIhuRsidcg) Google Doc for instructions on how to use this implementation to build and test mixed language targets.

author: ayazhafiz
body:
With fixpoint-fixing, we don't want to re-unify type variables that were just fixed, because doing so may change their shapes in ways that we explicitly just set them up not to be changed (as fixpoint-fixing clobbers type variable contents).

However, this restriction need only apply when we re-unify two type variables that were both involved in the same fixpoint-fixing cycle. If we have a type variable T that was involved in fixpoint-fixing, and we unify it with U that wasn't, we know that the $U \notin \bar{T}$, where $\bar{T}$ is the recursive closure of T. In these cases, we do want to permit the usual in-band unification of $T \sim U$.

Certain device level functions originate from instance level extensions such as vkSetDebugUtilsObjectName. The code to validate that functions queried with vkGetDeviceProcAddr did not properly handle this case, leading to nullptr being returned. This is hidden because the loader uses vkGetInstanceProcAddr to query debug utils functions, but layers such as renderdoc use vkGetDeviceProcAddr leading to calls to these functions never reaching the validation layers.

Fixes #4814

author: trellixvulnteam
body:
# Patching CVE-2007-4559

Hi, we are security researchers from the Advanced Research Center at [Trellix](https://www.trellix.com). We have began a campaign to patch a widespread bug named CVE-2007-4559. CVE-2007-4559 is a 15 year old bug in the Python tarfile package. By using extract() or extractall() on a tarfile object without sanitizing input, a maliciously crafted .tar file could perform a directory path traversal attack. We found at least one unsantized extractall() in your codebase and are providing a patch for you via pull request. The patch essentially checks to see if all tarfile members will be extracted safely and throws an exception otherwise. We encourage you to use this patch or your own solution to secure against CVE-2007-4559. Further technical information about the vulnerability can be found in this [blog](https://www.trellix.com/en-us/about/newsroom/stories/research/tarfile-exploiting-the-world.html).

If you have further questions you may contact us through this projects lead researcher [Kasimir Schulz](mailto:kasimir.schulz@trellix.com).

author: emilk
body:
`RERUN_MEMORY_LIMIT=1GB RERUN_TRACK_ALLOCATIONS=1 cargo r -- ../objectron.rrd` ->

![Screen Shot 2022-11-21 at 23 04 48](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/1148717/203167357-08fcd414-589b-4aaa-a503-43b122bd4bec.png)

This PR adds an opt-in allocation tracker, feature-gated by the environment variable `RERUN_TRACK_ALLOCATIONS=1`. It tracks all allocations over 128 bytes, grouping them by their backtrace. This lets us show a summary of which callstacks are responsible for most memory allocation.

This slows down execution quite a lot (at least 10x), but is great for finding different types of memory leaks (e.g. caches that are never purged, or ever-growing channels).

### Future work
Since our current data store is based around `BTreeMap` we get a lot of small allocations (e.g. 192 bytes), and we also get different backtraces depending on how deep the `BTreeMap` had to recurse before doing an allocation. This is a downside of the backtrace method of grouping allocations. It could be solved by some pre-processing of the callstacks (e.g. removing recursive calls).

author: nithinp7
body:
Fixes #95 
Changes:
- Overrides Unity's object focusing behavior in the editor so that it is more consistent and usable for tilesets.
- Changed the "Place Origin Here" behavior to preserve the forward direction of the camera wrt the globe from before the georeference change.
- Exposes functions on the `CesiumGeoreference` to transform direction vectors between ECEF and Unity World.

An easy way to test the old vs new behavior is to add two far-apart tilesets like Denver and Melbourne. Double-click on the further one and then hit "Place Origin Here". Repeat for the other tileset.

The specific mechanism by which I overrode Unity's focusing behavior is a bit hacky, so I'll explain it here briefly. So Unity provides a way to override a gameobject's apparent bounding volume - this overriden bounding volume is what gets used for Unity's built-in focusing functionality. If we simply provide a custom Unity bounding volume (converted from the root tile's ECEF bounding volume), then the camera might awkwardly get positioned _below_ the terrain when focusing a tileset on the other side of the Earth (Unity will not understand the local "up" direction). 

So we want to construct the camera focus transform ourselves, which we can do using the `SceneView` API. However, there is no clear way to get notified on the hierarchy double-click event, and there is no way to explicitly override the default focusing behavior that happens on double-click (apart from custom bounds as mentioned above). So instead what we do is the following:
- Detect when the `SceneView` _wants_ to focus on the tileset (`SceneView` will invoke `OnGetFrameBounds` to request custom bounds).
- Run our custom focusing logic, which updates the `SceneView`.
- Return dummy bounds with an infinite extent so that the editor's attempt to focus will _silently fail_. Otherwise our camera update will be squashed by an incorrect transform.

If anyone finds a more elegant way going forward absolutely feel free to throw this hack away, but it seems to work well for now!

body:
#### Summary
Currently, there's no easy way for the user to go back to Launchpad after they have made changes in the site editor. This PR creates a Modal that opens every time the user saves a change.

#### Testing instructions:
There are two possibilities for testing this - testing on the local jetpack docker setup or testing it on WPCOM by using `jetpack rsync`

##### Notes:
You should already have setup your local jetpack environment. I've [followed these instructions](https://github.com/Automattic/jetpack/blob/trunk/tools/docker/README.md#quick-install-wordpress) for the docker setup

##### Testing on WPCOM
1. Create a new Link in Bio site
2. Checkout this branch
3. Run `jetpack watch` and select `plugins -> jetpack`
4. Run `jetpack rsync` to sync your local changes to your sandbox ([Fieldguide page](PCYsg-eg0-p2))
5. Connect to your sandbox. You should see your changes applied.
6. Sandbox `public-api.wordpress.com` and your site URL
7. Go to `YOUR_SITE/wp-admin`
8. Go to the site editor (Appearance -> Editor)
9. Make a change in the site editor and click "Save"
10. You should see the Launchpad modal appear
11. Clicking "Back to Edit" or the close button should close the modal
12. Clicking "Launch Site" should take you to the Launchpad screen

**NOTE:** You might have to include `define( 'JETPACK_BETA_BLOCKS', true );` in your sandbox `wp-config.php`. This has been flaky for me, initially it didn't work without it but now it does so I'm not sure if this is required for an extension plugin...

body: Adds optional `chunk_length` parameter to `timeslide_injections` project. If passed, will chunk segments longer than `chunk_length` to avoid loading too much data into memory.

author: tonijbaker
body:
Tabloid Web-API 
Trello Ticket #20
https://trello.com/c/BH4IHw5v/20-20-create-a-comment

Files Modified:
Backend:

new file CommentRepository  AddComment();
new file ICommentRepository  AddComment();
new file CommentController Line 39-49 [HTTP POST)

Frontend:
New file CommentNew.js
PostDetails Lines 81-89 conditional for navigation to /my-posts/${id}/addComment or /posts/${id}/addComment

1.git add and git commit whatever you're working on on your branch
2.git checkout main
3.git fetch --a (or git fetch --all)
4.git checkout tbAddCommentToPost to switch to my branch.
5.If you don't see the most recent version of the files, try git pull origin tbAddCommentToPost
6.If you haven't created the Tabloid database, please do so.
7.Use this to fill out tables and columns: [SQL data](https://github.com/NewForce-Cohort-6/tabloidfullstack-stuffing/blob/main/SQL/01_Tabloid_Create_DB.sql)
8.Use this to seed the database: [SQL Seed Data](https://github.com/NewForce-Cohort-6/tabloidfullstack-stuffing/blob/main/SQL/02_Tabloid_Seed_Data.sql)
9.In your terminal, navigate to the client folder (something like cd workspace/Tabloid/Tabloid/client)
10.If you have not run the command npm install in your terminal at this folder level, do so now.
11.Go back to Visual Studio. Execute the backend of Tabloid from inside of Visual Studio by clicking on the solid green arrow.
12.A browser running Swagger should pop up.
13.In your terminal, run the command npm start
14.A browser tab running Tabloid should appear.
15.Login as ryakushkev4@weibo.comx
16. navigate to Posts in header
17. select a single post to view post details
18. at bottom of post details select add new comment
19. you should be directed to form for adding a new comment with a subject and content.  Enter information and save, 
20. you should be directed to the full comments list for that single post with the current date.
21. Repeat steps 16-20 for My Posts in Header
22. Logout
